speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a neck swelling. To begin my assessment, how long have you noticed this lump, and has it changed in size recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Thyroid (or Metastatic Colon Cancer to the Neck/Thyroid).

Given your history of colon cancer and this painless, progressive swelling on the nape of your neck for two months, I am highly concerned about metastatic disease to the thyroid or lymph nodes. I will need to see a CT scan of your neck with contrast to evaluate the extent of the mass and check for distant spread. REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_CT_with_contrast. Additionally, please undergo a fine-needle aspiration biopsy of the lump. REQUEST TEST: Fine_needle_aspiration_biopsy_of_neck_mass.
